notes: Hard rules — read carefully and respect in full:

(1) DO NOT modify WT_KSP_LOGK, WT_SOLID_PHASE, or WT_HYDROLYSIS_LOGK unless the minteq.v4.dat file at the pinned SHA-256 a93914e63b0c616f8506cc92739188e50c5b9a15c33b111979652f308457f4ac directly contradicts the constant. The pre-investigation hypothesis that constants might be stepwise rather than cumulative is to be verified and the finding reported, not pre-emptively acted on. The pre-fix check at capacityAtSaturation() expects: for Pb at pH 9, free ion = 10^(-19.83 - 2*(9-13.99)) = 10^-9.85 = 1.41e-10 mol/L; for Zn at pH 9, free ion = 10^(-15.506 - 2*(9-13.99)) = 10^-5.526 = 2.98e-6 mol/L.

(2) The pre-existing 5/6 failures must NOT be hidden by relaxing tolerance, inverting assertions, or marking expected values as 'noted to differ from PHREEQC'. Every changed expectation must trace to either the PHREEQC reference output or a documented solver formula evaluation.

(3) The filtrate operator change (max(0, input - capacity) -> min(input, capacity)) is the only change to capacity.ts that the chemistry owner has already implicitly authorized by signing off the user's Lỗi B diagnosis. The accompanying comment must explain the chemistry: capacity is the dissolved concentration at saturation, not the precipitable amount. Mass conservation is enforced by min(), which says 'the dissolved part of an undersaturated or saturated influent equals the smaller of input and equilibrium capacity'.

(4) WT_CAPACITY_TABLE column identity must be verified before any change. The pre-investigation check is: for each row, compute free ion = 10^(logKsp - valence*(pH-13.99)) for both Zn and Pb Ksp values and see which matches the 'pb' column. The check is expected to show the 'pb' column equals Zn free ion. The 'zn' column is expected to match neither Zn nor Pb Ksp free ion; investigate the source value before correcting.

(5) The pH passed to capacityAtSaturation() in the golden test is the EQUILIBRATED pH from the PHREEQC select.out (G2: 8.78, G3: 9.92), not the initial pH written in the .pqi comment. This is because the closed-form solver evaluates at one pH, and the PHREEQC reference that the test must match is the post-equilibration state. Document this in the report and in the test comment.

(6) G1 is AI-prepared and has no PHREEQC select.out. After the operator fix, evaluate G1 with the SOLVER at pH 7.5 (the .pqi is the only source) and report whether the resulting filtrate is consistent with the 'filtrate giữ nguyên input' claim. If inconsistent, mark G1 as 'unverified — needs live PHREEQC run' rather than inventing a reference value.

(7) The P0-F status (đã đóng 17/10/2026) is NOT re-opened by this task. The chemistry owner sign-off remains valid; only the formula and the cited expected values within the report are corrected. Add a new section in P0-F-CROSSCHECK-REPORT.md titled 'Errata (17/10/2026)' to record the corrections.

(8) Diff must touch only files in the 'files' allowlist. Use git diff --stat against base 73d4932 to confirm. Any change to AGENTS.md, package.json, vitest.config.ts, or any other source outside the allowlist is a scope violation and must be reverted before handoff.

These come from tools/research/phreeqc-pin/3.8.6-17100/actual/GC-SOLID-01.select.out. If web cannot read the file, record that in result.limits.
